contract.definition: A binding agreement between two or more persons that is enforceable by law.

agreement.definition: The statement (oral or written) of an exchange of promises.

terms.definition: (usually plural) a statement of what is required as part of an agreement.

conditions.definition: (usually plural) a statement of what is required as part of an agreement.

clause.definition: A separate section of a legal document (as a statute or contract or will).

amendment.definition: A formal change made to a legal document or agreement.

addendum.definition: An additional section or document attached to an existing agreement.

breach.definition: A failure to perform some promised act or obligation.

void.definition: Lacking any legal or binding force.

complaint.definition: A document setting out a claimant's allegations and requested remedy in a civil case.

summons.definition: An order to appear in person at a given place and time.

subpoena.definition: A legal order requiring someone to give evidence or provide specified documents.

motion.definition: A formal request asking a court to make a decision or take an action.

brief.definition: A written document presenting legal arguments and relevant facts to a court.

petition.definition: A formal written request asking a court or authority to act.

order.definition: A legally binding command or decision entered on the court record (as if issued by a court or judge).

injunction.definition: (law) a judicial remedy issued in order to prohibit a party from doing or continuing to do a certain activity.

warrant.definition: A written court order authorizing a specified action, such as a search or arrest.

indictment.definition: A formal document written for a prosecuting attorney charging a person with some offense.

will.definition: A legal document stating how a person's property should be handled after death.

trust.definition: A legal arrangement in which someone manages property for another person.

power-of-attorney.definition: A formal document gives a chosen person authority to make decisions or take actions for the person who grants it.

living-will.definition: A document recording a person's wishes about future medical treatment if they cannot communicate.

deed.definition: A legal document signed and sealed and delivered to effect a transfer of property and to show the legal right to possess it.

title.definition: The legal right to own property.

lease.definition: An agreement allowing property to be used for a period in return for payment.

prenuptial.definition: Relating to an agreement made by a couple before marriage.

divorce-decree.definition: A court order that formally ends a marriage and may set out related legal decisions.
divorce-decree.exampleUsage: The lawyer placed the certified divorce decree in the case file.

adoption-papers.definition: Legal documents used to record and complete an adoption under the relevant legal process.
adoption-papers.exampleUsage: The court file contained the completed adoption papers.

patent.definition: A legal right allowing an inventor to control use of an invention for a limited period.

trademark.definition: A name, symbol, or sign used to identify a business's goods or services.

copyright.definition: Legal protection for original creative work, such as writing, music, or art.

license.definition: An official document giving permission to do something.

nda.definition: A non-disclosure agreement, usually called an NDA, is a legal contract that binds its parties to keep specified confidential information secret.

non-compete.definition: A contract term that restricts certain competitive work or business activity after or during a relationship; enforceability varies by jurisdiction.
non-compete.exampleUsage: The employee asked a lawyer to explain the non-compete clause.

partnership-agreement.definition: A contract setting out how a business partnership will operate, including responsibilities, ownership, and decision-making.
partnership-agreement.exampleUsage: The partners reviewed the partnership agreement with legal counsel.

articles-of-incorporation.definition: A legal filing creates a corporation under government authority and sets out its basic structure and rules.

bylaws.definition: A rule adopted by an organization in order to regulate its own affairs and the behavior of its members.

operating-agreement.definition: A document that sets rules for the ownership and management of a limited liability company in jurisdictions that use this form.
operating-agreement.exampleUsage: The company kept its operating agreement with its legal records.
